reason: The cited evidence (E2, E3) directly demonstrates phase-selective recrystallization in a eutectic HEA, showing it eliminates weak boundaries and achieves high ductility (~35% uniform elongation) with high strength (~2 GPa true stress), fully supporting all key premises. E1 provides only general background on dual-phase HEAs and is not essential for the specific premises.
premises: Phase-selective recrystallization of the soft phase in a dual-phase eutectic alloy is feasible.
Recrystallizing the soft phase eliminates weak internal boundaries.
Eliminating weak boundaries reduces dislocation pile-ups and stress concentrations.
Reducing stress concentrations delays microcrack initiation and enhances ductility.
The hard phase skeleton is preserved during this treatment, retaining strength.
